items.title: The in-memory counter never forgets an address
items.why: Every address ever asked for stays in the Map: nothing deletes old keys, so memory grows with each new address until the process restarts.
items.comment: `hits` only gains keys: after 60 s an address's entry is filtered to `[]` but never deleted, so 1 000 000 distinct addresses keep 1 000 000 keys. Was a TTL sweep (or deleting empty keys) considered, or is a restart per deploy the plan?

evidence.detail: `private readonly hits = new Map<string, number[]>()` — no `hits.delete(` anywhere in src/reset/

items.confirm_by: `grep -rn "hits.delete" src/reset/` returns nothing; heap snapshot after `node scripts/try-reset.js --distinct 100000`
items.unknown: Whether the author relies on deploy restarts to clear the Map

items.title: A bare 429 may make clients retry at once
items.why: With no wait time in the answer, a client that retries on 429 retries right away and hits the cap again.
items.comment: The cap answers `429` with no `Retry-After`. If the web client retries on 429, a user who taps 4 times waits a full 60 s with no hint. Is the header planned for slice 2, or should this slice send `Retry-After: 60`?

evidence.detail: the client code is not in this repo; retry-on-429 behaviour is a guess

items.confirm_by: `grep -rn "429" web/src/api/` in the client repo shows whether it retries
items.unknown: Whether any client retries automatically on 429

decisions.risk_if_wrong: cap × instances; memory grows per address
decisions.cost_to_undo: low — swap the Map for a shared store

decisions.risk_if_wrong: clients retry at once and stay capped
